Large language model (LLM) agents keep a long-term memory that the model itself writes: summaries, extracted facts and em-
beddings derived from what users said. Deleting a message is therefore not enough: its derivatives, storage residue and backups
survive. We definelineage-complete forward-secure erasure: after a forget request, an adversary that later obtains all storage and
the agent's current keys learns nothing about the forgotten input or any memory derived from it. We present LinEra, which encrypts
each memory under a key derived from its parents' keys along the derivation graph; source keys come from a puncturable pseu-
dorandom function, so forgetting is a single puncture and every descendant becomes unreadable without being located. Asound
lineage rule records as parents everything the writer saw, which confines all influence of a source to its descendants. We prove
security

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using objective adversarial security tests and standard benchmark question-answering metrics without metric-driven feedback loops.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective cryptographic leak analysis (exact matching, raw byte scanning, vector decoy ranking), token F1 on QA benchmarks, and runtime benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; LinEra is a cryptographic key-derivation and storage mechanism, not an optimized or trained ML model.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The theoretical claims are supported by proofs, and the empirical results demonstrate the trade-offs between context window size, fan-in, and utility loss, matching the derived fan-in law without fitted parameters.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The experimental evaluation tests canary secret leakage across four channels on LoCoMo and LongMemEval with multiple open LLM writers (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-7B) and integrates with mem0. LinEra completely prevents canary leakage where baselines leak heavily, empirically verifies the fan-in forgetting law, and assesses downstream QA utility and system latency up to 10^6 objects.

evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective cryptographic leak analysis (exact matching, raw byte scanning, vector decoy ranking), token F1 on QA benchmarks, and runtime benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; LinEra is a cryptographic key-derivation and storage mechanism, not an optimized or trained ML model.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss limitations, including plaintext leakage of the lineage graph structure, restriction to models up to 7B parameters, dependence on seeing full prompt contexts, and the necessity of re-derivation or small-context writing to mitigate utility loss.
primary.method_assessment: LinEra combines a GGM tree-based puncturable PRF with HKDF key derivation across object parent graphs and ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, with vector index sharding. Formal proofs of LC-FS security and lineage integrity are provided in both random-oracle and standard models, clearly establishing the cryptographic guarantees.
primary.quality_rationale: The work presents a rigorous cryptographic definition, sound proofs, a functional reference implementation, and thorough empirical experiments exploring security and utility trade-offs without overclaiming.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formalizes lineage-complete forward-secure (LC-FS) erasure for LLM agent long-term memory and proposes LinEra, a cryptographic system deriving keys along the lineage DAG using a puncturable PRF so that a single puncture renders an input and all its derived memories undecryptable. It also analyzes the resulting forgetting radius and evaluates remedies (re-derivation and windowed writing).
